question: due_diligence
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
where_to_look: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144): https://leg.colorado.gov/laws/session-laws/SB26-144/135/download
note: No statewide statutory due-diligence instruction to buyers was found; county treasurers' pages carry 'buyer beware' warnings (see county rows).

question: deposit
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
where_to_look: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144): https://leg.colorado.gov/laws/session-laws/SB26-144/135/download
note: SB 26-144 lets the treasurer require a deposit from the lawful holder applying for a deed (39-11.5-102(5)); no statewide bidder deposit was found. Check the county treasurer's bidding rules.

question: extra_costs
answer: If the property is sold to a third-party bidder, or to the lawful holder bidding competitively, the treasurer may collect up to three hundred dollars from the successful bidder for processing the public auction.
quote: IF A PROPERTY IS SOLD TO A THIRD-PARTY BIDDER OR A LAWFUL HOLDER AS A COMPETITIVE BIDDER, A TREASURER MAY COLLECT UP TO THREE HUNDRED DOLLARS FROM THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FOR PERFORMING ACTIONS RELATED TO PROCESSING THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: how_it_works
answer: After a tax lien has been held long enough, the lawful holder of the certificate of purchase may apply for a treasurer's deed; the county treasurer then holds a public auction, and the winning bidder receives a certificate of option for a treasurer's deed.
quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED IN THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... "CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED" MEANS A CERTIFICATE ISSUED BY A TREASURER TO THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: liens_survive
answer: Subject to junior lienors' overbid claims, title is free and clear of liens and encumbrances junior to the certificate of purchase. The treasurer's deed does not affect existing roads, rights-of-way, conservation easements, other easements or equitable servitudes.
quote: THE TITLE IS FREE AND CLEAR OF ALL LIENS AND ENCUMBRANCES JUNIOR TO THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... EXECUTION OF A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION DOES NOT AFFECT THE EXISTENCE OF ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE ROADS, RIGHTS-OF-WAY, CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, OTHER EASEMENTS, OR EQUITABLE SERVITUDES
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: opening_bid
answer: The lawful holder must bid no less than the total debt as determined by the treasurer; the bid form sets out all money due to the lawful holder, including the treasurer's fees and costs.
quote: MUST SET FORTH ALL MONEY DUE AND OWING TO THE LAWFUL HOLDER, INCLUDING ALL TREASURER FEES AND COSTS ... A LAWFUL HOLDER MUST BID NO LESS THAN THE AMOUNT OF THE TOTAL DEBT, AS DETERMINED BY THE TREASURER, FOR THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE BEING SOLD.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: pay_after_win
answer: Payment of the amount bid must reach the treasurer by the date and time of the auction, or at another time on the auction day that the treasurer sets in writing, in the form the treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder does not pay in full, the next highest bidder who pays in time is the successful bidder.
quote: THE PAYMENT OF ANY AMOUNT BID AT AN AUCTION MUST BE RECEIVED BY A TREASURER NO LATER THAN THE DATE AND TIME OF THE AUCTION, OR AT AN ALTERNATIVE TIME AFTER THE AUCTION AND ON THE DAY OF THE AUCTION, AS SPECIFIED IN WRITING BY THE TREASURER. A BID PAYMENT MUST BE MADE IN THE FORM SPECIFIED BY THE TREASURER.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: The property owner may redeem before the auction by filing an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction. After the auction, a lawful holder who did not win may repurchase the certificate of option by noon on the eighth business day after the auction.
quote: A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM ... NO LATER THAN NOON ON THE EIGHTH BUSINESS DAY FOLLOWING THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER MAY REPURCHASE THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: register
answer: The statutory notice of public auction tells interested bidders that they must register and gives the treasurer's website or office phone number for more information.
quote: INTERESTED BIDDERS MUST REGISTER. MORE INFORMATION AT (WEBSITE OR TREASURER'S OFFICE PHONE NUMBER).
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: schedule
answer: The first public auction must be scheduled no less than thirty and no more than sixty calendar days after the treasurer mails the notice of public auction.
quote: THE INITIAL PUBLIC AUCTION HELD PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE 11.5 MUST BE SCHEDULED FOR NO LESS THAN THIRTY CALENDAR DAYS NOR MORE THAN SIXTY CALENDAR DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF MAILING THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: unsold
answer: If no valid bids are received at the public auction, the lawful holder who does not withdraw the application becomes the purchaser.
quote: "PURCHASER" MEANS A PERSON TO WHOM THE TREASURER AWARDS THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED AS THE WINNING BIDDER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION WHO TIMELY SUBMITS PROPER FUNDS, OR, IF NO VALID BIDS ARE RECEIVED AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER WHO DOES NOT FILE A WITHDRAWAL OF THE APPLICATION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: what_you_get
answer: When the repurchase period ends, title vests in the holder of the certificate of option, and the treasurer executes and records a treasurer's deed confirming the transfer.
quote: UPON THE EXPIRATION OF THE REPURCHASE PERIOD ... TITLE TO THE PROPERTY VESTS IN THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... THE TREASURER SHALL EXECUTE AND RECORD A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO SECTION 39-11.5-502 TO THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... CONFIRMING THE TRANSFER OF TITLE TO THE PROPERTY.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: where_when
answer: The treasurer holds the public auction at a courthouse or at a building housing the county clerk and recorder or the treasurer, as named in the notice; it may also be held on the internet or another electronic medium.
quote: THE TREASURER SHALL CONDUCT THE PUBLIC AUCTION AT ANY DOOR OR ENTRANCE TO, OR IN ANY ROOM IN ANY BUILDING TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY USED AS, A COURTHOUSE OR AT OR WITHIN ANY BUILDING WHERE THE OFFICE OF THE COUNTY CLERK AND RECORDER OR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER IS LOCATED, WHICH PLACE MUST BE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED IN THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION; EXCEPT THAT A PUBLIC AUCTION MAY ALSO BE CONDUCTED BY MEANS OF THE INTERNET OR OTHER ELECTRONIC MEDIUM.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: expiry
answer: A certificate of purchase lien may not remain a lien longer than seven years after issuance (the rule does not apply to certificates held by the county). A certificate issued before January 1, 2026 may remain a lien for fifteen years.
quote: No lien upon property created by a certificate of purchase issued by a treasurer on account of any delinquent property taxes or any special assessment MAY remain a lien for a period longer than SEVEN years after the issuance thereof ... NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS SECTION, A LIEN ON PROPERTY CREATED BY A TAX LIEN SALE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 1, 2026, MAY REMAIN A LIEN FOR A PERIOD OF FIFTEEN YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF ISSUANCE.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: As amended by SB 26-144: the session law strikes 'fifteen' and adds 'SEVEN'; quoted with struck words omitted (read from the printed page).

question: how_to_buy
answer: Tax liens are sold to the bidders who pay the taxes, delinquent interest and fees, or who pay the largest amount above them (a premium); the excess goes to the county general fund.
quote: sold to the persons who pay therefor the taxes, delinquent interest, and fees then due thereon or who further pay the largest amount in excess of said taxes, delinquent interest, and fees. The excess amount shall be credited to the county general fund.
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-115(1): 'shall' became 'MUST' in the last sentence; the rule is otherwise unchanged.

question: if_not_redeemed
answer: After August 1 of the third calendar year after the tax lien sale, the lawful holder may apply for a treasurer's deed. The property then goes to a public auction; if the holder is not the winning bidder, the holder may repurchase the certificate of option within the repurchase period.
quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... A LAWFUL HOLDER IS ENTITLED TO REPURCHASE A CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED IF THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS ARE MET TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE TREASURER: (a) THE LAWFUL HOLDER WAS NOT THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.

question: interest_return
answer: Redemption interest is nine percentage points above the discount rate a commercial bank pays the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, rounded to the nearest full percent.
quote: The annual rate of redemption interest shall be nine percentage points above the discount rate, which discount rate shall be the rate of interest a commercial bank pays to the federal reserve bank of Kansas City using a government bond or other eligible paper as security, and shall be rounded to the nearest full percent.
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: Read from the 2024 C.R.S. title 39 printout (the newest posted); SB 26-144 (2026) does not amend this section.

question: redemption_period
answer: The owner may redeem at any time before a treasurer's deed is executed. Under the treasurer's deed auction process, the owner must file an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction.
quote: The redemption may be made at any time before the execution of a treasurer's deed ... A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM THE PROPERTY WITH THE TREASURER.
source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
note: 39-12-103(3) quoted from the 2024 C.R.S. printout (https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-39.pdf), not amended by SB 26-144; 39-11.5-106 from the SB 26-144 session law.

question: what_is_it
answer: The treasurer prepares a certificate of purchase for the purchaser of a tax lien on real property sold for delinquent taxes; it describes the property and states the rate of interest and the total taxes, delinquent interest and fees.
quote: The treasurer shall prepare, sign, and retain for safekeeping or deliver to the purchaser of a tax lien on any real property sold for the payment of delinquent taxes a certificate of purchase describing the property on which the taxes and fees were paid by the purchaser, as the same was described in the record of sales, and also stating the rate of interest and the total amount of all taxes, delinquent interest, and fees
source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-117 (wording only); quoted words are unchanged.

question: office
answer: The Douglas County Treasurer's office handles the tax lien sale, county-held liens and treasurer's deeds: phone 303-660-7455, general information 303-660-7400.
quote: If you want to assign your purchase to another investor, contact our office at 303.660.7455 ... Treasurer Phone: 303-660-7455 ... General Info 303-660-7400
source_title: Tax Lien Sale Information - Douglas County

question: how_to_buy
answer: Douglas County's 2026 internet tax lien sale is held November 5, 2026 through zeusauction.com. It is a premium auction: the minimum starting bid is the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees, and bidders may bid above it; premiums are never returned and draw no interest.
quote: The 2026 Internet Tax Lien Sale will be held Nov 5th, 2026 ... The minimum starting bid for each tax lien certificate is equal to the amount of the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees as shown on the SRI internet auction website. Douglas County tax certificates sales are "PREMIUM" auctions in which a bidder can choose to bid up the minimum amount due. Premiums are never returned and draw no interest
source_title: Tax Lien Sale Information - Douglas County
note: Same page: 2026 interest is 13%; payment for winning bids is by ACH from the bank account given at registration.

question: office
answer: The Morgan County Treasurer (who also serves as Public Trustee) handles tax lien sales and treasurer's deed auctions: P.O. Box 593, Fort Morgan, CO 80701, phone 970-542-3518, Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
quote: County Treasurer Robert A. Sagel ... P.O. Box 593 Fort Morgan, CO 80701 970-542-3518 ... Office Hours Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
source_title: Treasurer and Public Trustee | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

question: pay_after_win
answer: The winning bid must be paid to the Morgan County Treasurer by noon on the sale day, in cash, cashier's check payable to the Morgan County Treasurer, bank check, or electronic transfer to an account the Treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder has not paid by noon, the next highest bidder who has paid in full by 2:00 p.m. is the successful bidder.
quote: Payment of any successful bid amount must be received by the Morgan County Treasurer no later than noon on the same day as the sale. If full payment of the bid amount from the highest bidder at the sale is not received by noon on the day of the sale, the next highest bidder who has tendered the full amount of their bid by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the auction shall be deemed the successful bidder
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: Accepted funds (same page): cash, a Cashier's Check payable to the Morgan County Treasurer, a bank check, or by electronic transfer to an account specified by the Treasurer.

question: register
answer: All bidders must register with the Morgan County Treasurer's office before the auction.
quote: All bidders must register with the Morgan County Treasurer's office prior to the auction
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

question: schedule
answer: Treasurer's deed option auctions are held on Wednesdays at 9:30 a.m.; auction dates are on the published notice and the Treasurer's website.
quote: Auctions are conducted on Wednesdays at 9:30 a.m. ... Auction dates can be found on the published notice and the Treasurer's website.
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: Page title: 'Auction for Certificate of Option for a Treasurer's Deed Bidding Rules and Information'. The page predates or does not cite SB 26-144; check it against the current statute.

question: where_when
answer: Auctions are held in person at the east front door of the Morgan County Administration Building; the Treasurer takes verbal bids from registered bidders or their agents who are present, in $5.00 minimum increments.
quote: at the east front door of the Morgan County Administration Building ... the Treasurer will entertain verbal bids from any registered bidders or their designated agents that are present. The minimum bid increment is $5.00.
source_title: Bidding Rules and Information | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky

question: how_to_buy
answer: Morgan County's tax lien sale is a premium auction held online: the bidder offering the highest premium above the tax lien buys it; the minimum premium is $1.00 and successful premium bids are not refunded.
quote: A premium bid is an amount over and above the tax lien being offered. Minimum premium bids are $1.00. If there are competing bids, the investor offering the highest premium bid purchases the tax lien. PLEASE BE AWARE THAT SUCCESSFUL PREMIUM BIDS ARE NOT REFUNDED.
source_title: Tax Lien Sale | Morgan County Where Prairie Meets the Sky
note: The page describes the 2025 sale (online at zeusauction.com, November 18-20, 2025). Unsold liens are held by the county and are normally available from the Treasurer's office (same page).

question: office
answer: The Saguache County Treasurer/Public Trustee handles tax lien sales and treasurer's deed auctions: PO Box 177, Saguache, CO 81149, phone 719-655-2656, email saguachetreasurer@saguachecounty-co.gov.
quote: For inquires and general information: saguachetreasurer@saguachecounty-co.gov ... PO Box 177 Saguache, CO 81149 Phone: 719-655-2656
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

question: extra_costs
answer: For treasurer's deed auctions, any current year's tax not endorsed before the auction is the responsibility of the party who receives the treasurer's deed.
quote: Any current year's tax that was not endorsed prior to the auction will be the responsibility of the parties to whom the Treasurer's Deed is issued.
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

question: pay_after_win
answer: For treasurer's deed auctions, bids are paid by wire transfer through the auction company.
quote: 3-Bids will be paid via wire transfer through the auction company.
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County
note: Treasurer's deed auction bidding rules; the page states no payment terms for the annual tax lien sale.

question: register
answer: Bidders register for the tax lien sale at zeusauction.com. For treasurer's deed auctions you must create a GovEase account and also register for the specific auction.
quote: Saguache County Tax Lien Sale accepts registration for bidders at www.zeusauction.com. ... You will need to create an account and register for the auction. Creating an account with GovEase.com will not automatically register you for an auction
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

question: schedule
answer: The annual tax lien auction will be held online November 2-4, 2026. Treasurer's deed auctions are held online every two weeks on Wednesdays at 10am, except holidays.
quote: Annual Tax Lien Auction will be held online, November 2-4, 2026. ... All Treasurer's Deed auctions will be held bi-weekly on Wednesday's at 10am, with the exception of holidays online
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County
note: The Saguache records on this site come from the County's 2026 tax lien sale list.

question: where_when
answer: The tax lien sale for real properties and minerals is online only, at zeusauction.com. Treasurer's deed auctions are online at GovEase; a workstation is available in the Treasurer's office.
quote: Real properties and Mineral Interest will be online only. ... All Treasurer's Deed auctions will be held bi-weekly on Wednesday's at 10am, with the exception of holidays online at; https://liveauctions.govease.com/co/cosaguachetread/1418/browsestandard ... A workstation is available in the Treasurer's office
source_title: Treasurer/Public Trustee | Saguache County

question: due_diligence
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, chapter 197 (Online Sunshine)
where_to_look: The 2026 Florida Statutes, chapter 197 (Online Sunshine): https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/0197.html
note: Chapter 197 contains no buyer due-diligence checklist; county clerks publish their own 'as is' / buyer-beware notices.

question: deposit
answer: The high bidder must post a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale; it is applied to the price at full payment.
quote: The high bidder shall post with the clerk a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale, to be applied to the sale price at the time of full payment.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)

question: extra_costs
answer: On top of the final bid, the buyer pays the documentary stamp tax and recording fees. At an electronic sale, the winning bidder's advance deposit is subject to the fee under s. 28.24(11).
quote: full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees ... The portion of an advance deposit from a winning bidder required by subsection (2) shall, upon acceptance of the winning bid, be subject to the fee under s. 28.24(11).
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)

question: how_it_works
answer: Property on which a tax deed application has been filed is sold at public auction to the highest bidder by the clerk of the circuit court of the county where the property is located.
quote: Real property advertised for sale to the highest bidder as a result of an application filed under s. 197.502 shall be sold at public auction by the clerk of the circuit court, or his or her deputy, of the county where the property is located
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)

question: liens_survive
answer: Except as the chapter provides, no right, interest, restriction or covenant survives the tax deed, but a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district or community development district that is not satisfied from the sale proceeds survives.
quote: Except as specifically provided in this chapter, no right, interest, restriction, or other covenant shall survive the issuance of a tax deed, except that a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district, or community development district, when such lien is not satisfied as of the disbursement of proceeds of sale under the provisions of s. 197.582, shall survive the issuance of a tax deed.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
note: F.S. 197.573 also keeps recorded use restrictions and covenants running with the land enforceable after a tax deed.

question: opening_bid
answer: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property, the opening bid is the value of all outstanding certificates plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. On property assessed as homestead on the latest roll it also includes one-half of the latest assessed value.
quote: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property shall be the sum of the value of all outstanding certificates against the property, plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes, if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. ... an amount equal to one-half of the latest assessed value of the homestead.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
note: Re-read 2026-10-29; same provision as the VERIFIED opening_bid rule in data/state_rules.csv. F.S. 197.502(6)(b) sets the opening bid on an individual's certificate.

question: pay_after_win
answer: Full payment of the final bid, documentary stamp tax and recording fees is due within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays. If it is not made, the clerk cancels all bids, readvertises the sale and pays the sale costs from the deposit.
quote: If full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees is not made within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays, the clerk shall cancel all bids, readvertise the sale as provided in this section, and pay all costs of the sale from the deposit.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: A certificate can be redeemed at any time before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk.
quote: A person may redeem a tax certificate at any time after the certificate is issued and before a tax deed is issued unless full payment for a tax deed is made to the clerk of the court, including documentary stamps and recording fees.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)

question: register
answer: The statute lets the clerk require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit, and at an electronic sale to advance enough funds to pay the deposit. Each county's own registration steps are in its county rows.
quote: the clerk may require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit ... electronic proxy bidding shall be allowed and the clerk may require bidders to advance sufficient funds to pay the deposit required by subsection (2).
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)

question: schedule
answer: The sale is held on the date, at the time and at the location set out in the published notice, during the clerk's regular office hours. The notice runs once a week for 4 consecutive weeks and no sale may be held until 30 days after the first publication.
quote: on the date, at the time, and at the location as set forth in the published notice, which must be during the regular hours the clerk's office is open ... the clerk shall publish a notice once each week for 4 consecutive weeks at weekly intervals ... No tax deed sale shall be held until 30 days after the first publication of the notice.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
note: Second and third quoted passages are from F.S. 197.512(1) (https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.512.html).

question: unsold
answer: If there are no higher bids the property is struck off to the certificateholder. If there are no bidders and the certificateholder does not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk puts the land on the list of lands available for taxes.
quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes"
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
note: F.S. 197.542(1): 'If there are no higher bids, the property shall be struck off and sold to the certificateholder'.

question: what_you_get
answer: The buyer receives a tax deed issued in the name of the county and signed by the clerk. The deed is prima facie evidence that all proceedings were regular, and the grantee is entitled to immediate possession.
quote: All tax deeds shall be issued in the name of a county and shall be signed by the clerk of the county. ... All deeds issued pursuant to this section shall be prima facie evidence of the regularity of all proceedings from the valuation of the lands to the issuance of the deed, inclusive.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
note: Immediate possession: F.S. 197.562 ('shall be entitled to the immediate possession of the lands described in the deed').

question: where_when
answer: A clerk may hold electronic tax deed sales instead of public outcry, with electronic proxy bidding allowed. The clerk must provide public computer terminals for the electronic sale at a designated location.
quote: A clerk may conduct electronic tax deed sales in lieu of public outcry. The clerk shall provide access to the electronic sale by computer terminals open to the public at a designated location.

question: how_to_buy

quote: During the first 90 days after the property is placed on the list, the county may purchase the land for the opening bid or may waive its rights to purchase the property. Thereafter, any person, the county, or any other governmental unit may purchase the property from the clerk, without further notice or advertising, for the opening bid

question: timeline
answer: Three years after the day the land was offered for public sale, unsold land escheats to the county free and clear, and the clerk executes an escheatment tax deed to the board of county commissioners.
quote: Three years after the day the land was offered for public sale, the land shall escheat to the county in which it is located, free and clear. All tax certificates, accrued taxes, and liens of any nature against the property shall be deemed canceled as a matter of law
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)

question: what_is_list
answer: These are properties offered at a tax deed sale that drew no bidders, where the certificateholder did not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days. The clerk enters them on the list of lands available for taxes and notifies the county commission.
quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes" and shall immediately notify the county commission that the property is available.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)

question: what_you_get

source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)

question: expiry
answer: Seven years after the certificate's issuance date (the first day of the advertised certificate sale), if no tax deed has been applied for and no other administrative or legal proceeding, including a bankruptcy, has existed of record, the certificate is null and void and canceled. This does not apply to deferred payment certificates.
quote: Seven years after the date of issuance of a tax certificate, which is the date of the first day of the tax certificate sale as advertised under s. 197.432, if a tax deed has not been applied for, and no other administrative or legal proceeding, including a bankruptcy, has existed of record, the tax certificate is null and void and shall be canceled.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.482 (Online Sunshine)
note: Resolves the UNRESOLVED certificate_term row in data/state_rules.csv.

question: how_to_buy
answer: Each certificate goes to the bidder who will pay the taxes, interest, costs and charges and demand the lowest interest rate, up to the maximum. Bids are in quarter-percent steps; unsold certificates are struck to the county at the maximum rate. The tax collector may require a deposit and may sell electronically with proxy bidding.
quote: Each certificate shall be awarded to the person who will pay the taxes, interest, costs, and charges and will demand the lowest rate of interest, not in excess of the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter. The tax collector shall accept bids in even increments and in fractional interest rate bids of one-quarter of 1 percent only.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.432 (Online Sunshine)
note: Same section: 'If a certificate is not purchased, the certificate shall be struck to the county at the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter'; (7) 'The tax collector may require payment of a reasonable deposit'.

question: if_not_redeemed
answer: After 2 years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, and before it is canceled, the holder may file the certificate and a tax deed application with the county tax collector. The property is then sold at public auction by the clerk.
quote: The holder of a tax certificate at any time after 2 years have elapsed since April 1 of the year of issuance of the tax certificate and before the cancellation of the certificate, may file the certificate and an application for a tax deed with the tax collector of the county where the property described in the certificate is located.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
note: The applicant also pays all other outstanding certificates, omitted, delinquent and current taxes and the costs of sale (F.S. 197.502(2)); the auction is under F.S. 197.542.

question: interest_return
answer: The maximum interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year. When interest earned at redemption is less than 5 percent of the face amount, a mandatory minimum of 5 percent applies, except on certificates bid at zero percent.
quote: The maximum rate of interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year. ... a mandatory minimum interest of an absolute 5 percent shall be levied upon the face value of the tax certificate. ... except those with an interest rate bid of zero percent.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.172 (Online Sunshine)
note: Second and third passages are from F.S. 197.472(2) (https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.472.html).

question: redemption_period
answer: A certificate may be redeemed at any time after it is issued and before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk. The redeemer pays the tax collector the face amount plus all interest, costs and charges.
quote: A person may redeem a tax certificate at any time after the certificate is issued and before a tax deed is issued unless full payment for a tax deed is made to the clerk of the court, including documentary stamps and recording fees. The person redeeming a tax certificate shall pay the tax collector the face amount plus all interest, costs, and charges.
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)
note: Resolves the UNRESOLVED redemption row in data/state_rules.csv.

question: what_is_it
answer: A tax certificate is a legal document representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, interest and related costs, issued against a specific parcel and becoming a first lien on it. The tax collector sells certificates on property whose taxes have not been paid.
quote: "Tax certificate" means a paper or electronic legal document, representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, including special assessments, interest, and related costs and charges, issued in accordance with this chapter against a specific parcel of real property and becoming a first lien thereon, superior to all other liens, except as provided by s. 197.573(2).
source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.102 (Online Sunshine)
note: Sale by the tax collector: F.S. 197.432(1).

question: deposit
answer: The tax collector may require registered participants to pay a deposit, not to exceed one thousand dollars, before the auction. The winner's deposit is applied to the sale price; other bidders' deposits are returned no later than fourteen days after the auction closes.
quote: The tax collector may require all registered tax lien auction participants to provide a deposit, not to exceed one thousand dollars, prior to the commencement of the tax lien auction. If a deposit is required, the deposit of the winning bidder shall be applied toward the sale price at the time of purchase. A deposit from a nonwinning bidder shall be returned or refunded to the depositor no later than fourteen days after the close of the auction.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153

source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154

question: how_it_works
answer: The tax collector advertises the tax lien for sale by public auction and issues a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder, recorded in the mortgage records.
quote: the tax collector will advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien and that the tax collector will issue in favor of the winning bidder and record in the mortgage records a tax lien certificate.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2153
note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

question: liens_survive
answer: A judicial sale to enforce the tax lien ends all interests in the property, except rights created by certain written instruments listed in the statute that were filed before the tax lien certificate was recorded.
quote: a judicial sale pursuant to R.S. 47:2267 shall terminate all interests in the immovable property. B. The rights and obligations established or created by the following written instruments affecting immovable property shall not be terminated pursuant to this Chapter to the extent the interests remain effective against third persons and are filed with the appropriate recorder prior to the recordation of the tax lien certificate:
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2268

question: opening_bid
answer: The auction price is the face value of the tax lien certificate. Bidders compete on the monthly interest rate: the maximum is one percent per month, bids go down in steps of one-tenth of one percent, and no bid below seven-tenths of one percent per month is accepted.
quote: The auction price shall be the face value of the tax lien certificate. ... Subject to a maximum bid of one percent per month, bidders may submit bids reducing the monthly interest rate in increments of one-tenth of one percent or an integral multiple thereof. ... no bid shall be accepted that purports to reduce the rate of monthly interest below seven-tenths of one percent.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154

source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2266.1

question: schedule

source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154

question: what_you_get
answer: After the later of three years from recording the tax lien certificate or six months after the required post-auction notices, a certificate holder may sue to have the delinquent obligation and the lien recognized.

source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2266.1
note: The winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, not a deed (R.S. 47:2154(E)); property passes only through the judicial sale in R.S. 47:2267, executed by the sheriff. question: expiry
answer: An action to enforce the tax lien must be brought within seven years from recording the tax lien certificate in the parish mortgage records; after that the tax lien is extinguished.
quote: An action to enforce the tax lien pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be brought no later than seven years from the date that the tax lien certificate is recorded in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is located. Upon the expiration of this time period, the tax lien shall be extinguished
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2155

question: how_to_buy
answer: Bidding is on the monthly interest rate that will accrue on the certificate's face value; the lowest rate wins, and a tie goes to the bidder who bid first.
quote: The subject of the competitive bidding shall be the monthly rate at which interest will accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate following its issuance. ... The bid that requires the assessment of interest at the lowest rate shall be declared the winner. If multiple bidders submit the same lowest bid, the winner shall be the first in time to submit the bid.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154

question: if_not_redeemed
answer: A judgment for the certificate holder in an enforcement action under R.S. 47:2266.1 is executed by a writ of fieri facias under the Code of Civil Procedure (a judicial sale).
quote: a judgment rendered in favor of the tax lien certificate holder in an action brought pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be executed by a writ of fieri facias in accordance with the provisions of Title II of Book IV of the Code of Civil Procedure
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2267

question: interest_return
answer: Interest accrues on the certificate's face value at the monthly rate set by the winning bid, or at one percent per month when the political subdivision holds the certificate, in both cases without compounding.
quote: Upon the issuance of a tax lien certificate, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the monthly rate established by the winning bid at the tax lien auction. If the tax lien certificate is issued in favor of the political subdivision, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the rate of one percent per month. In both cases, interest shall be calculated on a noncompounding basis.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154

question: redemption_period
answer: The taxes, interest, penalties and costs may be paid at any time until thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.
quote: the statutory impositions, together with interest, penalties, and costs, may be paid at any time prior to the expiration of thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2155

question: what_is_it
answer: At the tax lien auction the winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, recorded in the parish mortgage records, which is prima facie evidence of the lien and its assignment to the holder.
quote: No later than thirty days after conclusion of the tax lien auction, the tax collector shall issue and file in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is situated a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder. ... The tax lien certificate shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the tax lien and the assignment to the person named thereon.
source_title: Louisiana State Legislature - RS 47:2154
note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

question: office
answer: Sales of adjudicated property are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney, telephone (225) 389-3114.
quote: Abandoned adjudicated property sales for the Parish are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney. Questions concerning the sale process and procedures should be addressed to that office, telephone number (225) 389-3114
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

question: application
answer: To open a file: a completed 'Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property' form, the two-page tax print and current tax bill from the Sheriff, and a certified check or money order for advanced costs for each property, among other items.
quote: A completed "Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property" form . ... A copy of the two page tax print and the current tax bill for that particular property. You will obtain this from the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff. ... A certified check or money order for advanced costs for each piece of property you open a file on.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

question: extra_costs
answer: Advanced costs are at least $500 per property, and some properties have additional costs; this fee is not part of the sale price. The buyer also pays all fees and expenses to record the sale documents.
quote: This amount will be a MINIMUM of $500. However, each individual property may have additional amounts due for costs. ... This fee is not part of the sales price that is ultimately paid to buy the property. ... You are responsible for all fees and expense to record these documents.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

question: how_to_buy
answer: First confirm that the property was adjudicated and is still adjudicated to the City-Parish (the City-Parish keeps no list of adjudicated properties), then call the Parish Attorney's Office to confirm it is still available.
quote: you must first determine that the property in which you are interested has in fact been adjudicated, and is still adjudicated, to the City-Parish. The City-Parish does not maintain a roster/ list/ database of properties that are adjudicated. ... you must call the Parish Attorney's Office so that someone in our office can confirm that the property is still currently available
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
note: The Parish Attorney's own page also links an open-data list and CivicSource; the memorandum states the City-Parish keeps no list.

question: pay
answer: Advanced costs are paid by certified check or money order payable to the City of Baton Rouge (no personal checks or cash). The sale price is paid with certified funds at the closing.
quote: NO PERSONAL CHECKS OR CASH can be accepted. Checks must be made payable to the "City of Baton Rouge." ... Please note that you will be required to pay the sales price with certified funds at the time of the sale.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

question: price
answer: Offers need not equal the appraised value or the taxes and public liens; the Metropolitan Council considers those amounts when deciding whether to accept or reject the offer.
quote: Offers do not have to equal or exceed either the appraised value or the amount of taxes and public liens. However, these amounts will be considered by the Metropolitan Council at a regularly scheduled meeting in which it will be determined whether to accept or reject your offer.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

question: due_diligence
answer: Tax-Sale.info, which runs auctions for many Michigan county treasurers, says property is sold as is with no refunds and buyers must research a property before the auction.
quote: There are no refunds on property purchased at any of our auctions. All property is sold as is/where is and without warranty. It is the buyer’s responsibility to conduct research prior to the auction date and gain a full understanding of the property they intend to purchase.
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info
note: Applies to auctions conducted through Tax-Sale.info; the Michigan Department of Treasury notes many county treasurers hired Tax-Sale.info to conduct their auctions.

question: extra_costs
answer: Before the property is conveyed, the buyer must give the county proof of paying the local tax collecting unit any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.
quote: Before the foreclosing governmental unit conveys a property sold at a sale, the purchaser shall provide the foreclosing governmental unit with proof of payment to the local tax collecting unit in which the property is located of any property taxes owed on the property at the time of the sale.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: MCL 211.78m(10): 'The foreclosing governmental unit may charge a fee in excess of the minimum bid and any sale proceeds for the cost of recording a deed under this subsection.'

question: how_it_works
answer: Property foreclosed for delinquent taxes is sold at auction by the foreclosing governmental unit (or its authorized agent) at one or more sales, which may include an online auction.
quote: the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales at 1 or more convenient locations at which property foreclosed by a judgment entered under section 78k will be sold by auction sale, which may include an auction sale conducted via an internet website.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

question: liens_survive
answer: The foreclosure judgment extinguishes all existing recorded and unrecorded interests except, among others listed in the statute, a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, and the interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease.
quote: That all existing recorded and unrecorded interests in that property are extinguished, except a visible or recorded easement or right-of-way, private deed restrictions, interests of a lessee or an assignee of an interest of a lessee under a recorded oil or gas lease
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
note: 78k(5)(c) also keeps future installments of special assessments and environmental liens; 78m(12) cancels liens for demolition, safety repairs, debris removal and sewer or water charges as of the December 31 after the sale.

question: opening_bid
answer: The minimum bid must include all delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and fees on the property, and may include the foreclosing governmental unit's additional expenses for forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair or remediation.
quote: The minimum bid must include all of the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties, and fees due on the property, and may include any additional expenses incurred by the foreclosing governmental unit in connection with the forfeiture, foreclosure, maintenance, repair, or remediation of the property
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: At the final sale the minimum bid is not required; the county may set a reasonable opening bid to recover sale costs (MCL 211.78m(5)).

question: pay_after_win
answer: The county must require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date no more than 21 days after the sale.
quote: The foreclosing governmental unit shall require full payment at the close of each day's bidding or by a date not more than 21 days after the sale.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: All redemption rights expire on the March 31 after the foreclosure judgment is entered, or 21 days after the judgment in a contested case.
quote: All redemption rights to the property expire on the March 31 immediately succeeding the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section, or in a contested case 21 days after the entry of a judgment foreclosing the property under this section.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78k - Michigan Legislature
note: Former owners may instead claim remaining sale proceeds by filing a notice with the foreclosing governmental unit by the July 1 after foreclosure (MCL 211.78t(2)).

question: schedule
answer: Sales are held between the third Tuesday in July after the foreclosure judgment and the following first Tuesday in November.
quote: beginning on the third Tuesday in July immediately succeeding the entry of the judgment under section 78k vesting absolute title to tax delinquent property in the foreclosing governmental unit and ending on the immediately succeeding first Tuesday in November, the foreclosing governmental unit, or its authorized agent, at the option of the foreclosing governmental unit, shall hold 1 or more property sales
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

question: unsold
answer: By the December 1 after the judgment, a list of all unsold property goes to the clerk of the city, village or township where it lies, which may object in writing to the transfer of any of it.
quote: On or before December 1 immediately succeeding the entry of judgment under section 78k, a list of all property not previously sold by the foreclosing governmental unit under this section must be transferred to the clerk of the city, village, or township in which the property is located. The city, village, or township may object in writing to the transfer of 1 or more properties.
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature

question: what_you_get
answer: The deed must vest fee simple title in the highest bidder, unless the county finds a defect in the foreclosure or the sale is canceled.
quote: The deed must vest fee simple title to the property in the person bidding the highest amount above the minimum bid, unless the foreclosing governmental unit discovers a defect in the foreclosure of the property under sections 78 to 78l or the sale is canceled under this subsection or subsection (5).
source_title: MCL - Section 211.78m - Michigan Legislature
note: Tax-Sale.info's FAQ says buyers at its Michigan auctions receive a quitclaim deed.

question: how_to_buy

question: deposit
answer: To bid you must provide a $1000 pre-authorization on a major credit card; it is a hold, not a charge, and is collected only if you fail to pay for property you win.
quote: To place bids, you must be logged into a valid active account and must provide a $1000 pre-authorization on a major credit card. Pre-authorization is valid for 30-days. This pre-authorization is not a charge, but rather a hold by your financial institution for up to 30 days, which allows you to bid and serves as a security deposit. This hold will only be collected against if you fail to pay for property that you win.
source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Michigan Public Land Auction | Tax-Sale.info

question: extra_costs

question: how_it_works
answer: Before managing tax-forfeited land any other way, the county must first offer forfeited parcels at a public auction run by the county auditor and sell to the highest bidder.
quote: Prior to managing tax-forfeited lands as otherwise provided in this chapter, a county must first offer tax-forfeited parcels for sale pursuant to this section ... The county auditor must sell the property at a public auction to the highest bidder in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
note: Section added by 2024 c 127 art 70 s 4.

question: liens_survive
answer: Forfeiture extinguishes all liens, claims and encumbrances except: interested parties' rights to surplus proceeds, redemption rights under federal law, easements and rights-of-way of holders who are not interested parties, and recorded real covenants.
quote: The forfeiture of the property extinguishes all liens, claims, and encumbrances other than: (1) the rights of interested parties to surplus proceeds under this section; (2) rights of redemption provided under federal law; (3) easements and rights-of-way holders who are not interested parties; and (4) benefits or burdens of any real covenants filed of record as of the date of forfeiture.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: opening_bid
answer: The starting price is the estimated market value from the most recent assessment, and the property may not sell below it for 30 days. If no buyer pays it, the price drops to the minimum bid: the delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest and costs.
quote: "minimum bid" means the sum of delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interests, and costs assigned to the parcel. ... the initial price of the property, which is equal to the estimated market value, as determined by the most recent assessment. The property must not be sold for less than the initial price for 30 days after it is initially made available at auction. If no buyer is willing to pay the initial price, the price for the property must be reduced to the minimum bid.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: The law provides for repurchase by an interested party before the public sale, by paying all delinquent taxes and assessments with penalties, interest and costs.
quote: Prior to the public sale required under this section, an interested party may repurchase the property by payment of the sum of all delinquent taxes and assessments computed under section 282.251 , together with penalties, interest, and costs, that accrued or would have accrued if the parcel of land had not forfeited.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: schedule
answer: The sale must occur within six months of the filing of the certificate of forfeiture or the date the property is vacated, whichever is later, with notice published at least 30 days before the sale starts.
quote: The sale under this section must occur within six months of either the filing of the certificate of forfeiture pursuant to section 281.23, subdivision 9 , or the date the property is vacated by the occupant, whichever is later. Notice of the sale under this subdivision must be provided by publication in newspapers, websites, and other forums that serve diverse communities in the county where the property is located at least 30 days before the commencement of the sale.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: unsold
answer: If no buyer pays the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have bought the property by a credit bid, and the parcel may be disposed of under the rest of chapter 282.
quote: If no buyer is willing to pay the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have purchased the property through a credit bid and the parcels may be disposed of as otherwise provided in this chapter.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: what_you_get
answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued to the purchaser according to the land's status on forfeiture. Any conveyance of forfeited land reserves all minerals and mineral rights to the state.
quote: a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser as provided by the appropriate statutes according to the status of the land upon forfeiture. ... Any conveyance of forfeited lands shall be subject to exceptions and reservations in this state, in trust for the taxing districts of all minerals and mineral rights.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: where_when
answer: The law allows the public auction to be held online; a county may also sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction with posted and website notice at least ten days before it begins.
quote: in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction. ... may sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction. When an online auction is used to sell tax-forfeited lands, the county auditor shall post a physical notice of the online auction and shall publish a notice of the online auction on its website not less than ten days before the online auction begins
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: how_to_buy
answer: Remaining parcels are sold by the county auditor to anyone offering to pay the appraised value. A person who could have repurchased the parcel may not buy it for less than all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest and costs due at forfeiture.
quote: Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value, except that if the person could have repurchased a parcel of property under section 282.012 or 282.241 , that person may not purchase that same parcel of property at the sale under this subdivision for a purchase price less than the sum of all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, and costs due at the time of forfeiture
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: pay
answer: Cash only, unless the county board has adopted a resolution for sale on terms. On terms, at least ten percent is paid at purchase and the balance in no more than ten equal annual installments.
quote: The parcels must be sold for cash only, unless the county board of the county has adopted a resolution providing for their sale on terms, in which event the resolution controls with respect to the sale. When the sale is made on terms other than for cash only (1) a payment of at least ten percent of the purchase price must be made at the time of purchase, and the balance must be paid in no more than ten equal annual installments
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: price
answer: Parcels are appraised by the county board, and the sale may not be for less than the appraised value, except under the city-sale alternate procedure.
quote: Any parcels of land proposed to be sold shall be first appraised by the county board of the county in which the parcels lie. ... The sale must not be for less than the appraised value except as provided in subdivision 7a.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: timeline
answer: The sale continues until all parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws parcels from sale.
quote: The sale must continue until all the parcels are sold or until the county board orders a reappraisal or withdraws any or all of the parcels from sale.
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: what_is_list
answer: After all parcels in a county sale have been offered to the highest bidder, the county auditor sells any remaining parcels to anyone offering the appraised value.
quote: and shall sell them to the highest bidder, but not for a sum less than the appraised value, until all of the parcels of land have been offered. Then the county auditor shall sell any remaining parcels to anyone offering to pay the appraised value
source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

question: how_it_works
answer: Land on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent is subject to sale to discharge the tax lien, held on the fourth Monday in August each year.
quote: All lands, lots, mineral rights, and royalty interests on which taxes or special assessments are delinquent and unpaid are subject to sale to discharge the lien for the delinquent and unpaid taxes or unpaid special assessments as provided for in this chapter on the fourth Monday in August of each year.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.150 RSMo
note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.

question: liens_survive
answer: The deed is subject to claims for unpaid taxes, except unpaid taxes whose lien was inferior to the lien for which the land was sold.
quote: subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes except such unpaid taxes, existing at time of the purchase of said lands and the lien for which taxes was inferior to the lien for taxes for which said tract or lot of land was sold
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo

question: opening_bid
answer: At the first offering, if no one bids a sum equal to the delinquent taxes with interest, penalty and costs, the land is not sold and is offered again at the next sale.
quote: If at the first offering of sale of any tract of land or lot under the provisions of this law, no person bids therefor a sum equal to the delinquent taxes thereon with interest, penalty and costs
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.240 RSMo

question: pay_after_win
answer: The purchaser must pay the bid to the collector immediately. A purchaser who fails to pay forfeits a penalty of twenty-five percent of the bid, and the land is offered again.
quote: the purchaser at such sale shall immediately pay the amount of his bid to the collector ... In case the purchaser fails to pay his bid, the land shall be again forthwith offered for sale the same as if no sale had been made, and the purchaser so failing shall forfeit and pay for the use of the distributive county school fund of the county a penalty of twenty-five percent of the amount of his bid
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.280 RSMo

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: The owner, lienholder, occupant or others with an interest have an absolute right to redeem for one year after the sale, and a defeasible right until the purchaser acquires the deed.
quote: shall have the absolute right to redeem the same at any time during the one year next ensuing and shall continue to have a defeasible right to redeem the same until such time as the tax sale purchaser acquires the deed
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.340 RSMo
note: Third offering: RSMo 140.250.1 (ninety-day redemption); post-third-offering sales: RSMo 140.250.4 (no period of redemption).

question: register
answer: No sale is made to a person who is currently delinquent on taxes on other property and does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. A nonresident must file a written consent to the jurisdiction of the county's circuit court.
quote: no sale shall be made to any person or designated agent who: (a) Is currently delinquent on any tax payments on any property, other than a delinquency on the property being offered for sale, and who does not sign an affidavit stating such at the time of sale. ... A nonresident shall file with said collector an agreement in writing consenting to the jurisdiction of the circuit court of the county in which such sale shall be made
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.190 RSMo

question: schedule
answer: The sale is held in or next to the courthouse on the fourth Monday in August, starting at ten o'clock and continuing from day to day until all land is offered.
quote: will be sold at public auction to discharge the taxes, penalty, interest, and costs due thereon at the time of sale in or adjacent to the courthouse of such county, on the fourth Monday in August next thereafter, commencing at ten o'clock of said day and continuing from day to day thereafter until all are offered.
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.170 RSMo
note: Missouri ch. 140 is the general county tax sale law; St. Louis City and Jackson County collect delinquent land taxes under other chapters (ch. 92 / ch. 141), not read for these statewide rows.

source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.250 RSMo

question: what_you_get
answer: The collector executes a deed in the name of the state that vests an absolute estate in fee simple, subject to claims for unpaid taxes (other than certain inferior ones).
quote: The collector of the county in which the sale of such lands took place shall execute to the purchaser or the purchaser's heirs or assigns, in the name of the state, a conveyance of the real estate so sold, which shall vest in the grantee an absolute estate in fee simple, subject, however, to all claims thereon for unpaid taxes
source_title: Missouri Revisor of Statutes - Section 140.420 RSMo

quote: provides recommended purchase prices for lots and residential buildings. Note that all properties listed as "Appraisal" on the Price List, as well as any commercial/industrial buildings, may be sold for no less than 2/3 of their appraised value.
source_title: LRA Pricing Policy (Land Reutilization Authority, City of St. Louis)
