source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
where_to_look: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title): https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os68.rtf
note: No statewide deposit rule found for the June resale; see the county treasurer's resale instructions.

question: due_diligence
answer: County treasurers must make available to potential buyers at the resale the list of properties on which the Oklahoma Health Care Authority has liens.
quote: The county treasurers shall make the list of properties with the OHCA liens available to potential buyers at the tax resales.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: extra_costs
answer: In addition to the bid, the treasurer collects enough to pay the county's expenses of preparing, listing and advertising the property.
quote: The county treasurer shall also charge and collect from the purchaser at such sale an amount in addition to the bid placed on such real estate, sufficient to pay all expenses incurred by the county in preparing, listing and advertising the lot or tract purchased by such bidder
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: how_it_works
answer: When real estate taxes have been unpaid for three years or more, the county treasurer advertises and sells the real estate at the annual tax resale for those taxes and all other delinquent taxes, special assessments and costs.
quote: where taxes are a lien upon real property and have been unpaid for a period of three (3) years or more as of the date such taxes first became due and payable, advertise and sell such real estate for such taxes and all other delinquent taxes, special assessments and costs at the tax resale provided for in Section 3125 of this title
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
note: Oklahoma repealed its tax certificate sale sections in 2008 (Laws 2008, c. 82); 68 O.S. 3105.1 keeps earlier liens under the old law.

question: liens_survive
answer: The resale tax deed does not extinguish the mortgage of a mortgagee to whom no notice was sent.
quote: the resale tax deed shall be ineffective to extinguish any mortgage on said real estate of a mortgagee to whom no notice was sent.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
note: State claims: 68 O.S. 3131(A); covenants: 68 O.S. 3145.

question: opening_bid
answer: Property must sell for at least two-thirds of its current assessed value or the total taxes, penalties, interest and costs due, whichever is less.
quote: All property must be sold for a sum not less than two-thirds (2/3) of the assessed value of such real estate as fixed for the current fiscal year, or for the total amount of taxes, penalties, interest and costs due on such property, whichever is the lesser.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: pay_after_win
answer: Property is sold at public auction to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds; online auctions may accept online payments.
quote: The real estate shall be sold at public auction to the highest bidder for cash or certified funds. Online auctions may accept online payments.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: The owner or anyone with a legal or equitable interest may redeem only before the resale auction starts, by paying the original delinquency with interest and costs.
quote: may redeem the same at any time before the start of the resale auction by paying to the county treasurer the sum which was originally delinquent including interest at the lawful rate
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
note: Disability exception also in 68 O.S. 3131(A).

question: register
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
where_to_look: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title): https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os68.rtf
note: No statewide registration rule found; see the county treasurer's resale instructions.

question: schedule
answer: The resale is held on the second Monday of June each year; an online resale starts during normal business hours within the full week of the second Monday of June.
quote: the county treasurer shall proceed to sell such real estate at resale, which shall be held on the second Monday of June each year in each county or, if conducted through an online auction, shall be started on a date and time set by the county treasurer during normal business hours within the full week of the second Monday of June
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: unsold
answer: If no bid reaches the required minimum, the county treasurer bids the property off in the name of the county.
quote: if there is no bid equal to or greater than the sum so required, the county treasurer shall bid off the same in the name of the county.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: what_you_get
answer: The resale deed vests absolute and perfect title in fee simple, subject to all claims the state may have for taxes or other liens or encumbrances.
quote: shall vest in the grantee an absolute and perfect title in fee simple to the real estate, subject to all claims which the state may have had on the real estate for taxes or other liens or encumbrances
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
note: Surface rights: 68 O.S. 3119. No action to set aside the deed may begin twelve months after it is filed (3131(A)).

question: where_when
answer: The county treasurer may hold the June resale as an online auction instead of in person.
quote: The county treasurer may choose to hold the June resale through an online auction instead of the in-person process as prescribed in subsection A of this section.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: application
answer: The State Auditor and Inspector prescribes the form of bid the county treasurers use.
quote: The State Auditor and Inspector shall prescribe, for the use of the several county treasurers, a form of bid and form of report of sale.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: extra_costs
answer: Advertising and other sale expenses are added to the sale price as a separate charge paid by the purchaser in addition to the bid.
quote: The cost of the advertisement and other expense incident to the sale, as provided by law, shall be apportioned to the respective tracts listed in the sale and shall be added to the sale price of the real estate as a separate and additional charge and shall be paid by the purchaser, in addition to the amount bid upon the real estate.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: how_to_buy
answer: On the date in the published notice, the property is sold to the highest competitive bidder, or to the original bidder if no higher price is offered, subject to the board of county commissioners' approval.
quote: On the date stated in the notice, the property shall be sold by the county treasurer to the highest competitive bidder, for cash in hand or certified funds, or to the original bidder if there be no higher price offered. The sale in any event shall be subject to the approval of the board of county commissioners in its discretion.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: pay
answer: Bidders must pay a deposit before the property is advertised to cover advertising and costs.
quote: A deposit shall be required of any bidder before advertisement of the property to cover the advertisement and costs.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: price
answer: At a county auction, a bid below all the ad valorem taxes owed at the original resale is accepted only with the approval of the county commissioners and the county excise board.
quote: Any bid which is less than all of the real estate ad valorem taxes owed at the time of the original resale shall be accepted only upon approval of the county commissioners and the county excise board.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: timeline
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)
where_to_look: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title): https://www.oklegislature.gov/OK_Statutes/CompleteTitles/os68.rtf
note: No statutory time limit found; the county manages the property until sold (68 O.S. 3134).

question: what_is_list
answer: Property the county acquired at the tax resale may be sold by the county treasurer after notice by publication, at a price approved by the board of county commissioners.
quote: Any property acquired by the county under the provisions of the resale tax laws may be sold by the county treasurer, after notice by publication, at a price as may be approved by the board of county commissioners, the notice to be given after receipt of bid on the property.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: what_you_get
answer: After the commissioners approve the sale, their chair executes a deed conveying title on a form prescribed by the State Auditor and Inspector.
quote: Upon approval of the sale as hereinbefore provided, the chair of the board of county commissioners shall execute a deed conveying title to the purchaser of the property in as full and ample manner as by law provided on a form prescribed by the State Auditor and Inspector.
source_title: Oklahoma Statutes - Title 68 (Oklahoma Legislature, complete title)

question: office
answer: Questions about buying county property go to the Treasurer's delinquent tax department at (405) 713-1300.
quote: If you have any questions concerning this process, please call the delinquent tax department at (405) 713-1300.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - Guidelines for Purchasing County Owned Properties

question: extra_costs
answer: Successful bids include the cost, abstract fee and resale advertising; the Treasurer also collects $10.00 per deed plus a $20.00 filing fee.
quote: All Successful Bids include the amount bid and any cost, abstract fee, and Resale advertising. ... The Treasurer collect $10.00 for each deed issued and an additional filing fee of $20.00.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer

question: pay_after_win
answer: You must have cash at the time of the sale and cannot leave to get it; money can be placed on trust before 8:00 a.m. on sale day.
quote: YOU MUST HAVE CASH AT THE TIME OF THE SALE. YOU CAN NOT LEAVE TO GO GET CASH. YOU CAN PUT MONEY ON TRUST BEFORE 8:00 A.M. ON DAY OF SALE.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer

question: register
answer: Resale bidders must be 18 or older; for 2026 they could pre-register at the County Treasurer's Office from May 14 to June 5.
quote: ALL RESALE BIDDERS MUST BE 18 YEARS OF AGE OR OLDER, IN ORDER TO BID ON PROPERTY. ... Bidders can pre-register in the County Treasurer's Office May 14 thru June 5, 2026.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer

question: schedule
answer: The 2026 resale began Monday, June 8, 2026, between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., continuing day to day until completed.
quote: Beginning Monday, June 08, 2026, between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on Monday (Exact time to be determined by County Treasurer) and continuing from day to day thereafter between the hours of 8:00 a. m. and 5:00 p. m., until said sale has been completed according to law.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer
note: 2026 resale instructions; the next resale's dates are not yet published.

question: where_when
answer: Bidders must follow the sale on the Treasurer's Resale Active List web page.
quote: IT WILL BE THE BIDDERS RESPONSIBILITY TO FOLLOW ALONG WITH THE SALE FROM THE RESALE ACTIVE LIST ON OUR WEBSITE.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer

question: application
answer: A completed County Property Bid Form.
quote: An interested bidder must initiate a bid by completing a bid form
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - Guidelines for Purchasing County Owned Properties

question: extra_costs
answer: The Treasurer collects an additional $330.00 in cash for estimated publication cost, treasurer's cost and recording fees.
quote: We will collect an additional $330.00 in cash for estimated publication cost, treasurer's cost and recording fees.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - Guidelines for Purchasing County Owned Properties

question: how_to_buy
answer: Complete the County Property Bid Form, print it and present it to the Oklahoma County Treasurer's Office.
quote: An interested bidder must initiate a bid by completing a bid form by clicking this link, County Property Bid Form. You will need to print the form and present it to the Oklahoma County Treasurer's Office.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - Guidelines for Purchasing County Owned Properties

question: pay
answer: Pay the full bid in cash, or 10% in cash and the rest by personal check (proof it cleared is needed before the deed issues); cashier's checks and money orders are also accepted.
quote: Bidder has the option of paying full amount of bid in cash or paying 10% in cash with remaining balance to be paid by personal check (proof the check has cleared must be presented before deed will be issued). We also accept cashiers check or money orders.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer - Guidelines for Purchasing County Owned Properties

question: price
answer: Once the County owns these properties, the public can buy them through a bidding process.
quote: Once the County owns these properties, they can be purchased by the public through a bidding process.
source_title: Oklahoma County Treasurer

note: No statewide buyer due-diligence statement found in the Act; see the Fayette county row.

question: application
answer: The purchaser must give an affidavit with the information in section 502-A, including a statement that the purchaser is not delinquent in real estate taxes to any taxing district in Pennsylvania.
quote: The bureau shall require, as a condition of sale, that the purchaser provide an affidavit that includes the information specified under section 502-A. ... is not delinquent in paying real estate taxes to any taxing district in this Commonwealth
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(a), 502-A

question: extra_costs
answer: The bureau records the deed at the purchaser's expense. A county that has adopted the ordinance may also collect a fee of up to $250 from the buyer at the time of sale for its demolition and rehabilitation fund.
quote: It shall be the responsibility of the bureau to have the deed recorded at the expense of the purchaser. ... The governing body of a county may, by ordinance, impose a fee not to exceed two hundred fifty dollars ($250) for the sale of any property being sold in accordance with this act
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b), 631(b)

question: how_to_buy
answer: With the written consent of all taxing districts, the bureau may set a minimum purchase price and accept an offer at or above it without court approval. A taxing district may require the buyer to appear in person before its governing body.
quote: The bureau may, with the written consent of all the taxing districts where the property is located, establish a minimum purchase price and accept an offer of any price equal to or greater than the minimum purchase price for property placed in the "repository for unsold properties" without court approval and published notice of sale.
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(a) (72 P.S. 5860.627)

question: pay
answer: The property is conveyed upon payment of the agreed price.
quote: The property shall be conveyed to the purchaser upon payment of the agreed price
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b)

quote: establish a minimum purchase price and accept an offer of any price equal to or greater than the minimum purchase price
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)

question: what_is_list
answer: Property that remains unsold after being exposed to a judicial sale is placed in a "repository for unsold properties". The county tax claim bureau keeps the list and makes it available to the public during normal office hours.
quote: If, after conducting and exposing a property to a judicial sale under the provisions of this act, whether prior to, at the time of or after the effective date of this amendatory act, any property remains unsold, it shall be placed in a category to be termed "repository for unsold properties." A list of properties in this category shall be maintained by the bureau and shall be available during normal office hours to the general public.
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 626 (72 P.S. 5860.626)
note: Land banks (68 Pa.C.S. Ch. 21) are a separate program: a land bank must keep a public inventory of its property (68 Pa.C.S. 2110(a)).

question: what_you_get
answer: Repository property is conveyed free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, charges and estates of any kind, except ground rents separately taxed.
quote: The property shall be conveyed to the purchaser upon payment of the agreed price, free and clear of all tax and municipal claims, mortgages, liens, and charges and estates of whatsoever kind, except ground rents separately taxed.
source_title: Real Estate Tax Sale Law, Act of July 7, 1947, P.L. 1368, No. 542 (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
citation: Real Estate Tax Sale Law sec. 627(b)

quote: Tax Claim Bureau 2 West Main Street Uniontown PA 15401 Directions Phone 724-430-1208 Fax 724-491-2928 Hours Monday - Friday 8 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

question: application
answer: The bureau's checklist: one bid form, the Affidavit of Bidder(s), a money order, certified check or cashier's check for the bid amount, in an envelope marked "Sealed Repository Bid".
quote: CHECK LIST: ... ONE BID FORM ... AFFIDAVIT OF BIDDER(S) ... MONEY ORDER, CERTIFIED CHECK, OR CASHIER'S CHECK FOR BID AMOUNT ... ENVELOPE MARKED SEALED REPOSITORY BID

question: how_to_buy
answer: Repository properties can be bid on at any time by sealed bid. Bids are opened on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 a.m.; the municipality and school district accept or reject the bid, and the bureau notifies by mail within 30-45 days.
quote: If the property still does not sell, it is put on our Repository List and can be bid on at any time. We keep the sealed bids in a lockbox. We open the envelopes on the first Tuesday of the month at 10:00 a.m. It is the decision of the authorities to accept or reject your bid. (Municipality and School District) We will notify you by mail within 30-45 days of the decision.
source_title: Tax Sale Information | Fayette County, PA

quote: The successful purchaser, or assignee, is responsible for the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus documentary stamps necessary to be affixed and recording fees.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: how_it_works
answer: Real estate whose property taxes are delinquent is advertised and sold at public auction by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes. The advertisement is titled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
quote: The property duly advertised must be sold, by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes, at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county ... The property must be advertised for sale at public auction. The advertisement must be in a newspaper of general circulation within the county or municipality, if applicable, and must be entitled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

where_to_look: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws): https://www.scstatehouse.gov/code/t12c051.php

question: opening_bid
answer: The officer conducting the sale submits a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments and costs, including the taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
quote: shall submit a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to the amount of all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments including, but not limited to, assessments owed to a special taxing district established pursuant to Section 4-9-30, Chapter 19, Title 4, or an assessment district established pursuant to Chapter 15, Title 6, and costs including taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: pay_after_win
answer: The successful bidder must pay the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale, in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. A bidder who fails to pay has the bid cancelled and is liable for up to five hundred dollars in damages.
quote: for legal tender payable in full by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or money order on the date of the sale. ... The successful bidder at the delinquent tax sale shall pay legal tender as provided in Section 12-51-50 to the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes in the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale. ... The defaulting bidder is liable for no more than five hundred dollars damages upon default
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: Yes. The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months from the date of the sale. Interest on the bid runs from three percent (first three months) to twelve percent (last three months) and may not exceed the forfeited land commission's bid.
quote: The defaulting taxpayer, any grantee from the owner, or any mortgage or judgment creditor may within twelve months from the date of the delinquent tax sale redeem each item of real estate ... First three months three percent of the bid amount ... Last three months twelve percent of the bid amount However, in every redemption, the amount of interest due must not exceed the amount of the bid on the property submitted on behalf of the forfeited land commission pursuant to Section 12-51-55.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: schedule
answer: The sale is held on the advertised date. Real property must be advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the legal sales date.

source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: unsold
answer: The opening bid is made on behalf of the county forfeited land commission. The commission sells the lands bid in for it, on terms it decides are in the best interest of the county.
quote: shall effect the sale of lands forfeited and bid in for the various forfeited land commissions of the State by the county auditors or the tax collectors of the several counties of the State in pursuance of Section 12-51-55. All lands deeded to the forfeited land commission of any county shall be held by it as assets of the county and sold to the best interest of the county.
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 59 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: what_you_get
answer: If the property is not redeemed, the collector makes a tax title to the purchaser. The tax deed is prima facie evidence of good title, and after a further twelve months it is incontestable on procedural or other grounds.
quote: shall make a tax title to the purchaser or the purchaser's assignee. ... the tax deed issued is incontestable on procedural or other grounds. ... the deed of conveyance, whether executed to a private person, a corporation, or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: where_when
answer: The law requires a public auction at the courthouse or at another convenient place within the county, if that place is designated and advertised.
quote: at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county, if designated and advertised, on the advertised date
source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

question: how_to_buy

answer: Real property seized under a tax warrant or ordered sold after foreclosure of a tax lien is sold by the officer charged with selling the property. The sale is conducted the way similar property is sold under execution, except as the Tax Code provides otherwise.
quote: Real property seized under a tax warrant issued under Subchapter E , Chapter 33 , or ordered sold pursuant to foreclosure of a tax lien shall be sold by the officer charged with selling the property, unless otherwise directed by the taxing unit that requested the warrant or order of sale or by an authorized agent or attorney for that unit. The sale shall be conducted in the manner similar property is sold under execution
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: liens_survive
answer: A sale to a purchaser other than a taxing unit extinguishes each lien securing the delinquent taxes, penalties and interest included in the judgment. Title remains subject to restrictive covenants recorded before January 1 of the year the tax lien arose, a recorded lien under such a covenant not extinguished in the judgment, and valid easements of record (34.01(n)).
quote: a recorded restrictive covenant running with the land that was recorded before January 1 of the year in which the tax lien on the property arose, a recorded lien that arose under that restrictive covenant that was not extinguished in the judgment foreclosing the tax lien, and each valid easement of record … extinguishes each lien securing payment of the delinquent taxes, penalties, and interest against that property and included in the judgment
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). First quoted part from 34.01(n); second from 34.01(q)(1). The deed also remains subject to the defendant's right of redemption.

question: opening_bid
answer: The officer calculates the total amount due under the judgment: taxes, penalties and interest, any other amount awarded, court costs and the costs of the sale. If no bid sufficient to pay the lesser of that amount or the adjudged value is received, the taxing unit that requested the order of sale may end the sale.
quote: The officer shall calculate the total amount due under the judgment, including all taxes, penalties, and interest, plus any other amount awarded by the judgment, court costs, and the costs of the sale. … If a bid sufficient to pay the lesser of the amount calculated under Subsection (b) or the adjudged value is not received, the taxing unit that requested the order of sale may terminate the sale.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: pay_after_win
answer: Under the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure for execution sales, a bidder who fails to comply with the terms of the sale is liable to pay the plaintiff twenty percent of the value of the property plus costs, and the officer sells the property again.
quote: If any person shall bid off property at any sale made by virtue of an execution, and shall fail to comply with the terms of the sale, he shall be liable to pay the plaintiff in execution twenty per cent on the value of the property thus bid off, besides costs … When the terms of the sale shall not be complied with by the bidder the levying officer shall proceed to sell the same property again on the same day, if there be sufficient time
source_title: Texas Rules of Civil Procedure
note: Tax Code 34.01(a) applies execution-sale procedure to tax sales.

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: Yes. For a residence homestead or land designated for agricultural use, the owner may redeem on or before the second anniversary of the date the purchaser's deed is filed, paying the amount bid and other statutory amounts plus a 25% premium in the first year or 50% in the second. For other property the right must be exercised within 180 days after the deed is filed.
quote: may redeem the property on or before the second anniversary of the date on which the purchaser's deed is filed for record by paying the purchaser the amount the purchaser bid for the property … plus a redemption premium of 25 percent of the aggregate total if the property is redeemed during the first year of the redemption period or 50 percent … may be exercised not later than the 180th day following the date on which the purchaser's or taxing unit's deed is filed for record
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). The two-year rule in 34.21(a) applies to a residence homestead, land designated for agricultural use, or a mineral interest; 34.21(e) gives the 180-day period (premium not over 25 percent) for all other property.

question: register
answer: A commissioners court may require bidders to register with the county assessor-collector before the sale begins. The officer may not deliver a deed unless the purchaser shows an unexpired written statement issued by the county assessor-collector.
quote: A commissioners court may require that, to be eligible to bid at a sale of real property under this chapter, a person must be registered as a bidder with the county assessor-collector before the sale begins. … may not execute or deliver a deed to the purchaser of the property unless the purchaser exhibits to the officer an unexpired written statement issued under this section to the person by the county assessor-collector
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer). 34.015 applies in counties of 250,000+ that have not adopted 34.011, and in smaller counties that adopt it (34.015(p)). The statement costs at most $10 and expires on the 90th day after issuance (34.015(j), (k)).

question: schedule
answer: An in-person sale must take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month (the first Wednesday if that Tuesday is January 1 or July 4). An online auction may begin at any time but must conclude at 4 p.m. on that same day.
quote: must take place between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month or, if the first Tuesday of a month occurs on January 1 or July 4, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Wednesday of the month. (r-2) A sale of real property conducted by means of a public auction using online bidding and sale under Subsection (a-1) may begin at any time and must conclude at 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: unsold
answer: If no sufficient bid is received and the taxing unit does not end the sale, the officer bids the property off to the taxing unit that requested the order of sale, for the lesser of the judgment amount or the market value in the judgment. That taxing unit takes title for itself and the other taxing units in the suit.
quote: the officer making the sale shall bid the property off to the taxing unit that requested the order of sale … for the aggregate amount of the judgment against the property or for the market value of the property as specified in the judgment, whichever is less. … The taxing unit to which the property is bid off takes title to the property for the use and benefit of itself and all other taxing units that established tax liens in the suit.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: what_you_get
answer: The deed vests good and perfect title in the purchaser to the defendant's interest in the property, including the right to use and possess it, subject to the defendant's right of redemption (and the recorded covenants and easements listed in the statute). It may be impeached only for fraud.
quote: The deed vests good and perfect title in the purchaser or the purchaser's assigns to the interest owned by the defendant in the property subject to the foreclosure, including the defendant's right to the use and possession of the property, subject only to the defendant's right of redemption … The deed may be impeached only for fraud.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: where_when
answer: A tax sale must take place at the county courthouse, unless the commissioners court authorizes a public auction using online bidding and sale.
quote: The commissioners court of a county by official action may authorize the officer charged with selling property under this section to conduct a public auction using online bidding and sale. … Except as provided by Subsection (a-1) and this subsection, a sale of real property under this section must take place at the county courthouse in the county in which the land is located.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION

answer: A public resale requested by the taxing unit may be for any amount. A private sale under 34.05(h) may not be for less than the lesser of the market value in the judgment or the total judgments against the property.

question: timeline
answer: The taxing unit may sell the property at any time. If it has not sold the property within six months after the owner's right of redemption ends, any taxing unit entitled to the proceeds may ask the sheriff or a constable in writing to sell it at a public sale.
quote: If the purchasing taxing unit has not sold the property within six months after the date on which the owner's right of redemption terminates, any taxing unit that is entitled to receive proceeds of the sale by resolution of its governing body may request the sheriff or a constable in writing to sell the property at a public sale.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION
note: Read from the Texas Legislature's statute file server (statutes.capitol.texas.gov viewer).

question: what_is_list
answer: These are properties sold to a taxing unit at a tax sale. Such a taxing unit may sell the property at any time by public or private sale, subject to any right of redemption of the former owner; the redemption period begins when the deed to the taxing unit is filed for record.
quote: If property is sold to a taxing unit that is a party to the judgment, the taxing unit may sell the property at any time by public or private sale. … The sale is subject to any right of redemption of the former owner. The redemption period begins on the date the deed to the taxing unit is filed for record.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION

question: what_you_get

The conveyance shall be made subject to any remaining right of redemption at the time of the sale.
source_title: TAX CODE CHAPTER 34. TAX SALES AND REDEMPTION

question: what_is_it
answer: Texas does not sell tax lien certificates. The tax office sells no tax liens; the property itself is sold at the monthly tax foreclosure sale.

Note: The state does not sell tax lien certificates where a buyer becomes the lienholder for the back taxes.
source_title: Foreclosed properties frequently asked questions

question: how_it_works
answer: The county treasurer sells real property for delinquent taxes. The person who offers to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is the purchaser and receives a certificate of purchase from the treasurer.
quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof. ... the county treasurer upon payment of the fee provided by subparagraph (ix)(B) of this subsection shall make out, sign and deliver a certificate of purchase to the purchaser
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: liens_survive
answer: The certificate holder takes subject to special assessments for local or public improvements. The certificate or tax deed holder's lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.
quote: The holder of the certificate of purchase takes subject to any special assessments for local or public improvements. ... The lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: opening_bid
answer: The amount is the taxes, interest, penalties and costs due on the property, including the statutory charges.
quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: pay_after_win
answer: The purchaser must pay the county treasurer all amounts due immediately; otherwise the property is offered again and the original purchaser is disqualified.
quote: The purchaser shall immediately pay the county treasurer all amounts due on the real property in the absence of which the real property shall again be offered for sale and the original purchaser disqualified.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: redemption_after_sale
answer: Yes. The legal owner may redeem after the sale until a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer.
quote: Real property sold for delinquent taxes may be redeemed by the legal owner after the date of sale but before a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer pursuant to W.S. 39-13-108(e)(v)(A)
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)

question: schedule
answer: The sale is advertised once a week for three weeks in a legal newspaper, with the first publication at least four weeks before the sale and before the first week in September. Sales run between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded, and may be adjourned day to day until all lands are sold.
quote: he shall advertise notice of all sales of real property by publication thereof, once a week for three (3) weeks in a legal newspaper in the county, the first publication to be at least four (4) weeks prior to the day of sale and prior to the first week in September. ... between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded, and may be adjourned from day-to-day until all lands are sold
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)

question: unsold
answer: Property that cannot be sold for the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is bid in for the county. The county commissioners may sell and assign those certificates at public or private sale at any time; after four years the treasurer issues a tax deed to the county for unredeemed certificates it holds.
quote: Any real property which cannot be sold for the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs shall be bid in for the county by the county treasurer. ... The county commissioners of any county may sell and assign any certificate of purchase for real property bid in for the county ... at public or private sale at any time.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: what_you_get
answer: The buyer first receives a certificate of purchase. The treasurer issues a tax deed for unredeemed property 4 to 6 years after the sale on proper application; the tax deed is prima facie evidence of title, subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.
quote: The county treasurer shall accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale ... the deed is prima facie evidence of title to the property described subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: where_when
answer: Sales of real property are held at the county courthouse or county building.
quote: Sales of real property shall be held at the county courthouse or county building between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Sundays excluded
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: expiry
answer: The treasurer accepts tax deed applications no more than six years after the original sale. An action to enforce the certificate holder's lien may be started no earlier than four and no later than ten years after the sale.
quote: not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale for taxes ... No action provided by this section may be commenced less than four (4) years nor more than ten (10) years from the date of the original tax sale.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14). The statute does not use the word 'expire'; these are its time limits.

question: how_to_buy
answer: The statute names as purchaser any person who offers to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs due; it does not describe premium or interest bid-down bidding.
quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14). How a county chooses among several such persons is not stated in the statute; check the county treasurer.

question: if_not_redeemed
answer: The holder applies to the treasurer, returns the certificate of purchase, pays the fees and proves the required notice was given - including a notice served at least three (3) months before the application on each person in possession and on the person in whose name the property was taxed.
quote: upon proper application, return of the certificate of purchase, payment of fees and proof of compliance with the notice requirements of this section ... That at least three (3) months prior to the application a written or printed notice was served on each person in actual possession or occupancy of the real property and the person in whose name the property was taxed
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: interest_return
answer: On redemption the holder receives the sale amount plus 3%, plus interest at 15% per year since the sale for property sold at the 1982 tax sale and later; subsequent taxes the holder paid also earn 15% per year.
quote: The amount for which the property was sold at the tax sale ... plus: (I) Three percent (3%); plus (II) Interest at eight percent (8%) per annum since the date of sale except fifteen percent (15%) per annum on all property sold at date of 1982 tax sale and thereafter.
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: redemption_period
answer: The legal owner may redeem after the sale until a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted; the treasurer accepts tax deed applications no less than four years after the sale.
quote: may be redeemed by the legal owner after the date of sale but before a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer ... accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).

question: what_is_it
answer: The tax sale buyer receives a certificate of purchase describing the property, the taxes and costs paid and any special assessments. Certificates may be assigned by endorsement.
quote: The certificate of purchase shall describe the real property purchased, taxes and costs paid and shall state the amount of any special assessments for local or public improvements. Certificates of purchase may be assigned by endorsement
source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
